The Simpsons.text: Matt Groening named the family after his own, putting in Bart for himself; "Simpson" sounded like "simpleton".
The Simpsons.evidence: He created a dysfunctional family and named the characters after his own family members, substituting Bart for his own name; he thought Simpson was a funny name in that it sounded similar to "simpleton".

Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.text: Mariska Hargitay's Olivia Benson is the longest-running regular character in US primetime live-action drama.
Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.evidence: The two longest-running regular characters in primetime live-action scripted American television history both achieved that record on SVU. ... In fall 2021, Mariska Hargitay began her 23rd season as Olivia Benson, in turn breaking Belzer's record.

Law & Order.text: NBC brought it back in 2022 after an 11-year break, picking up with season 21.
Law & Order.evidence: On September 28, 2021, after an 11-year hiatus, NBC announced that the series would be revived for a 21st season, which premiered on February 24, 2022.

Family Guy.text: Fox canceled it, then revived it in 2004 after strong DVD sales and reruns; it has aired ever since.
Family Guy.evidence: Fox announced that the show had been canceled in May 2000, at the end of the second season. ... Favorable DVD sales and high ratings from syndicated reruns since then convinced Fox to revive the show in 2004; ... the show has remained on the air ever since.

NCIS.text: It began as two episodes of JAG in 2003 and was first titled Navy NCIS, which says "Navy" twice.
NCIS.evidence: Two episodes of JAG season eight, "Ice Queen" and "Meltdown", serve as the backdoor pilot of NCIS itself. ... The series originally had the redundant title Navy NCIS

Grey's Anatomy.text: Its title mixes heroine Meredith Grey's surname with Gray's Anatomy, the classic anatomy textbook.
Grey's Anatomy.evidence: Its title is a mixture of the protagonist's surname and the name of the classic human anatomy textbook Gray's Anatomy.

American Dad!.text: The Smiths share their home with Roger, an alien, and Klaus, a goldfish.
American Dad!.evidence: The show centers around the Smiths, a dysfunctional family consisting of parents Stan and Francine, their children, Hayley and Steve, as well as a goldfish named Klaus and an extraterrestrial named Roger.

Gunsmoke.text: It began on radio in 1952 and ran 20 TV seasons and 635 episodes, the record until The Simpsons.
Gunsmoke.evidence: Gunsmoke began in 1952 as a radio series. ... ran from September 10, 1955, to March 31, 1975, on CBS, with 635 total episodes. Airing for 20 seasons, it was the longest-running American primetime TV series until it was surpassed by The Simpsons.

Lassie.text: CBS dropped it partly because airing whole NFL games would push it out of its traditional 7 p.m. slot.
Lassie.evidence: CBS executives felt Lassie would not be well received in a time slot other than its traditional 7:00 p.m. slot, and, with the network's other family programs set, along with network being forced to air late afternoon football games in their entirety during the fall months beginning in 1970 as part of its contract with the NFL, the show was canceled.

Criminal Minds.text: It ended in 2020 after 15 seasons, then returned on Paramount+ in 2022 as Criminal Minds: Evolution.
Criminal Minds.evidence: Criminal Minds originally culminated after its fifteenth season on February 19, 2020; however, it was revived and re-titled Criminal Minds: Evolution for its sixteenth season, which premiered on Paramount+ in November 2022.
